title: Ramp Sprint: Sell-through Drill & Objection Sprint
summary: Internal enablement session focused on rapid sell-through scenarios, objection handling for Dedicated vs Hosted, and two live roleplay demos (low-latency pitch, cost-conscious pitch). Practiced handoffs to SE, agreed next steps to produce two short demo clips and an objection cheat-sheet.
topics: Positioning: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security and compliance rebuttals (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
Demo variants: low-latency customer vs cost-first customer
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nair, Amir Patel, Jordan Miles + roleplayers

-- Auto Summary (auto gen, messy) --
Quick drills, two roleplays. Several callouts: emphasize predictable throughput for Dedicated, call out KV cache + batching as cost wins, and peppy one-liner for Hosted. Security questions: can do V P C peering, KMS integration, SOC two in progress (sic). Action: make two 90s demo clips, send pricing cheat sheet, schedule quick pilot scoping.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Alright team, let's get started. Thanks for making time — we have a packed sprint. We're gonna run two 20 minute roleplays, a short objection sprint and then capture next steps. Amir, quick context for the reps?
[00:18] Amir: Yeah uh we're looking at reps who are mid-market, some growing up into enterprise. The ask is super practical: how do you close when they push back on cost, or on private deployment needs. We want crisp one-liners and a handoff motion to SE.
[00:35] Jordan: Also a reminder, some of these folks push on compliance early — SSO, SAML, audit logs — so include that.
[00:44] Liam: Cool. My aim in the roleplays is to keep the demo tight — 90 seconds to show the key differentiator, then hand off to SE for capacity/throughput Qs. We'll have a low-latency variant and a cost-optimized variant.
[01:05] Priya: Quick note, sometimes the reps muddle "KV cache" into "K V cache" or even "K V C" which confuses the security folks. Try: "we use prefix and KV caching to reduce tail latency and token cost". Short and visual.
[01:25] Speaker 4: (laughs) yep I've heard the "K V C" one live, painful.
[01:30] Maya: Ok first roleplay - Jordan will play a mid-market product lead, Liam you'll be the rep, Priya you'll jump in as SE after the handoff. Ready?
[01:45] Liam: I'm ready. [acts] Hi, Jordan, thanks for taking a minute. Quick Q — what's your current model latency SLA and token bill look like?
[01:59] Jordan: We're 300–450ms on average, but spikes are killing product usage. Cost is manageable but getting higher as usage scales. We don't want to re-architect infra.
[02:12] Liam: Totally. We typically pitch Hosted for fast time-to-value and Redwood Dedicated when customers need predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. For spikes, we show canaries and fallbacks across regions, and we can set model routing policies so critical requests hit lowest-latency pools.
[02:31] Jordan: What about data residency? We have EU-only users.
[02:36] Liam: Great callout — we can route by region and host EU-only model capacity, or run Private in your VPC for strict residency. I'll bring Priya in to talk throughput.
[02:46] Priya: Right, on throughput — our Dedicated pools are reserved GPU capacity; you get predictable p99 latency and we tune batching. Also prefix caching reduces repeated token work for stable prompts which can cut per-token cost materially.
[03:04] Jordan: How do you handle audit and key management?
[03:08] Priya: We integrate with KMS/HSM for customer-managed keys, and all admin activity can be logged for audit. SOC two is in our compliance pack, and we can share the security folder.
[03:20] Jordan: (interrupting) Whoa, SOC two? Is that in prod?
[03:24] Maya: It's in progress - small slip — we should say "SOC 2 Type II in progress, controls in place, paper trail available". Don't overpromise.
[03:33] Jordan: Ok, fair.
[03:35] Liam: Objection sprint moment — say the prospect pushes "we can get cheaper on spot GPUs elsewhere". How do we answer?
[03:42] Amir: Quick rebuttal: cheaper at raw hardware is not the whole story — include cost of ops, model tuning, and reliability. Redwood's value is predictable throughput + lower unit cost after you factor in KV caching, batching, and our routing fallbacks. Also, reserved capacity contracts avoid surprise spikes.
[04:02] Speaker 4: (murmur) hmm
[04:08] Jordan: Another common push: "we can't expose our data, we need air-gapped on-prem".
[04:12] Priya: We have Private/on-prem options, full control plane in your VPC, and an audit stack. For extreme air-gapped environments we have an on-prem package but that triggers a different procurement cycle. Be honest about timelines.
[04:29] Liam: Good. Let's run the second roleplay: cost-sensitive buyer. Maya you're the buyer, Jordan will observe.
[04:36] Maya: (sigh) Alright, I'm cost-focused and I say "Your price per token is higher than X vendor".
[04:42] Liam: Acknowledge then reframe: "Totally — pricing at the model/token level is one factor. Where we win repeatedly is predictable TCO: you reduce tail spend via caching, you avoid engineering lift to manage batching and kv caches, and with Dedicated you get lower unit cost at scale. Can we run a quick pilot to model real spend against your traffic?"
[05:04] Maya: They might say no to a pilot.
[05:06] Liam: Then offer a lightweight benchmarking — 48-hour sample with ephemeral data, we run two scenarios and give a delta.
[05:14] Jordan: (interrupt) Make sure reps know to ask for current token volumes — too many come in blind.
[05:19] Priya: Also important: show the math on a single slide: tokens/day x p50 latency cost vs projected with caching. Visual beats talk.
[05:27] [00:05:30] Speaker tag glitch - Speaker 2 appears as Speaker 1 for a short bit
[05:35] Amir: Quick coaching tip — keep the initial pitch to 30 seconds. Have two scripts: 1) low-latency hero; 2) cost-savings hero. Swap in one-liners: "Redwood makes inference predictable — consistent latency, measurable unit economics".
[05:57] Jordan: Let's record those two 30-second scripts. Liam, do yours.
[06:02] [00:06:02] Liam: Low-latency script: "When latency matters, we route to dedicated pools tuned for your model and sequence length. We also use prefix caching to preserve responsiveness for repeat prompts; for high-demand endpoints we can provide p99 SLAs."
[06:20] [00:06:20] Liam: Cost script: "When cost is the priority, we recommend Dedicated with quantization profiles and workload-aware batching; combined with KV caching you can see up to 40% per-token savings on stable prompts." (note: number illustrative)
[06:42] Maya: Good. Now the objection about "you don't support our custom model architecture" — a common one.
[06:48] Priya: We should say: "We have a model catalog and verified performance profiles; if you have a custom model we'll run a compatibility pass and propose an optimized kernel path or compatible variant. We can run a short benchmark to validate."
[07:02] Jordan: Let's practice a harder push: "We need to keep all inference in our VPC and cannot share any control plane".
[07:10] Priya: Acknowledge and be explicit: "We offer Private deployments where the control plane sits behind your VPC and we can also support an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements. That typically requires enterprise licensing and a slightly longer procurement timeline."
[07:26] Maya: (note) emphasize procurement timeline and resource needs — helps set expectations and avoid surprise stalls.
[07:33] [00:07:33] (phone buzz in background)
[07:40] Liam: Quick demo switch — we'll run a micro-demo script for token trimming. Show a before/after where prefix caching avoids re-synthesizing context. Jordan, you'll play the product manager to prompt it.
[07:52] Jordan: Alright demo. (roleplay) "User asks for a 20-step walkthrough, then repeats step 12 twice".
[08:01] Liam: (demo narration) "With naive serving we'd re-run from scratch; with prefix and KV caching we re-use the cache so latency and token cost drop significantly. Visual: show radar chart of latency and token spend".
[08:20] Maya: Little transcription glitch — our slide says "KV cache" but sometimes the demo overlay displays 'cache miss' incorrectly, make sure to pre-run demos.
[08:30] Priya: Also tip: keep the console UI to two clicks. Don't show logs unless asked.
[08:38] Amir: Objection sprint — competitor named OnyX (mis-transcribed sometimes) comes up, reps ask how we're different from Anthropic/OpenAI.
[08:48] Priya: High level: Anthropic/OpenAI are model-first; Redwood is inference-first — our value is predictable serving, cost controls, and multi-deployment options. Avoid deep model claims.
[09:02] Jordan: Do we have an updated competitive one-pager? Reps sometimes hand out stale comparatives.
[09:07] Maya: We'll update the one-pager. Action: Maya to own the updated competitive sheet.
[09:11] [00:09:11] Quick timer beep - we hit 9 minutes into the transcript chunk
[09:16] Roleplay block continues - reps practice quick closes and hand-offs
[09:30] Liam: Close script: "If you'd like, we can scope a 2–4 week pilot using a small Dedicated pool or Hosted with traffic mirroring to quantify both latency and cost. Which would you prefer to start with?"
[09:46] Jordan: Buyer: "I don't have time for long pilots."
[09:50] Liam: Offer 48-hour benchmark as a compromise.
[09:55] Maya: We did a rapid poll — reps liked the 48-hour benchmark idea. Put that in the playbook.
[10:00] [00:10:00] (audio label swapped: Liam now shows as Speaker 1 intermittently)
[10:12] Amir: Quick coaching on SLAs — don't promise p99 until procurement and SRE sign-off. Use phrasing "we can work with you on SLA targets as part of Dedicated contracts".
[10:26] Priya: Primer: what to do if prospect asks for heavy fine-tuning support — note that fine-tuning is handled by our applied ML team and requires an SOW. Surface that early to set expectation.
[10:40] Jordan: Let's take a fast feedback loop — what parts of the scripts felt weak?
[10:44] Maya: The cost script needed a cleaner punchline. The 40% number is illustrative; reps want a safe-range and a slide showing the math.
[10:54] Amir: Also reps sometimes bury the Private option in the middle of the pitch. Make Private a clear alternative: "If compliance is a blocker, we have Private/VPC and on-prem paths — let's validate the timeline and procurement path now."
[11:10] [00:11:10] small crosstalk, someone says "uh-huh"
[11:14] Liam: Ok final block — lightning round objections: "We already built an internal solution", "We already have discounts with cloud provider", "Your SLAs aren't strong enough". Quick rebuttals?
[11:24] Priya: For internal build: reframe on time-to-market and operational cost; for cloud discounts: ask for real spend numbers and show TCO; for SLAs: commit to working with procurement — highlight fallbacks and multi-region capabilities.
[11:40] Jordan: Let's capture final next steps and owners.
[11:45] Maya: Action items and next steps recap.

-- End of live transcript portion --

Notes on quality: automated transcription had moderate errors around acronyms (KV, VPC, KMS) and some speaker labels swapped mid-file. There's natural filler, crosstalk, and roleplay tagging.
